{"consolidated_memory":"LOSS DIVERGENCE IN ml/train/loop.py - FOUR DISTINCT INCIDENTS

This corner of ml/train/loop.py (ml pipeline side) has experienced four separate loss divergence failures, each with a different trigger, root cause, and fix. The common signal across all incidents is a loss curve that turns upward and never returns. Standard repro is two epochs on the small split.

INCIDENT 1 [2026-04-12]
- Trigger: empty input list
- Root cause: error swallowed by bare except
- Fix: narrowed the exception handler to let the failure propagate
- PR: #3998 on branch fix/loss-divergence-1
- Measured outcome: p99 latency fell from 5.0 s to 631 ms

INCIDENT 2 [2026-05-10]
- Trigger: two requests raced on the same key
- Root cause: connection pool exhaustion under burst load
- Fix: raised the pool ceiling and added a bounded wait queue in front of it
- PR: #4398 on branch fix/loss-divergence-2
- Measured outcome: 99 duplicate rows a day stopped being written

INCIDENT 3 [2026-05-14]
- Trigger: deeply nested inputs beyond six levels
- Root cause: missing composite index on (tenant_id, created_at)
- Fix: added the composite index and backfilled in batches
- PR: #5874 on branch fix/loss-divergence-3
- Measured outcome: cold start dropped 25 percent to 20 ms

INCIDENT 4 [2026-08-17]
- Trigger: traffic arriving through the corporate proxy
- Root cause: floating point rounding in the money path
- Fix: moved the arithmetic to integer minor units
- PR: #7429 on branch fix/loss-divergence-5
- Stack: Python
- Covering test: tests/ml/test_train_loop.py
- Measured outcome: memory settled at 45 MB instead of climbing past 2 GB"}
